q: The chemical compounds found in living things are referred to as _____ compounds due to their link with organisms.
e: The chemical compounds found in living things are referred to as organic compounds due to their link with organisms. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The enormous molecules termed _____ are formed by smaller molecules connecting together as if they were holding hands.
e: The enormous molecules termed macromolecules are formed by smaller molecules connecting together as if they were holding hands. An ether has an oxygen between two carbon groups, C-O-C.

q: Carbohydrates, proteins, and nucleic acids are natural polymers, while plastics are a type of _____ macromolecules manufactured in the industry.
e: Carbohydrates, proteins, and nucleic acids are natural polymers, while plastics are a type of synthetic macromolecules manufactured in the industry. A polymer is a long chain made by linking many small monomers.

q: The simplest organic compounds that contain only the elements carbon and hydrogen are called _____.
e: The simplest organic compounds that contain only the elements carbon and hydrogen are called hydrocarbons. A hydrocarbon contains only carbon and hydrogen.

q: An ether is an organic compound with an O atom bonded to two _____ groups.
e: An ether is an organic compound with an O atom bonded to two alkyl groups. Ethers have an oxygen bridged between two carbon groups and are often used as solvents.

q: In a symmetrical ether, the two alkyl groups are the _____.
e: In a symmetrical ether, the two alkyl groups are the same. Ethers have an oxygen bridged between two carbon groups and are often used as solvents.

q: Ethers have the general formula _____.
e: Ethers have the general formula CnH2n+2O. An ether has an oxygen between two carbon groups, C-O-C.

q: In the IUPAC system, the oxygen atom and the smaller alkyl group of an ether are named as an _____ substituent.
e: In the IUPAC system, the oxygen atom and the smaller alkyl group of an ether are named as an alkoxy substituent. Ethers have an oxygen bridged between two carbon groups and are often used as solvents.

q: Ethers can be obtained from alcohol by the elimination of a molecule of water from two molecules of alcohol at _____ °C.
e: Ethers can be obtained from alcohol by the elimination of a molecule of water from two molecules of alcohol at 140 °C. An ether has an oxygen between two carbon groups, C-O-C.

q: There is no intermolecular hydrogen bonding between ether molecules, which makes their boiling points much _____ than alcohol of similar molecular mass.
e: There is no intermolecular hydrogen bonding between ether molecules, which makes their boiling points much lower than alcohol of similar molecular mass. Intermolecular forces tug neighbouring molecules or ions together; they are not the bonds inside a molecule.

q: Ethers with up to _____ carbon atoms are soluble in water.
e: Ethers with up to three carbon atoms are soluble in water. An ether has an oxygen between two carbon groups, C-O-C.

q: On heating with concentrated hydrogen iodide (HI), the C-O bond in ethers breaks forming alcohol and _____.
e: On heating with concentrated hydrogen iodide (HI), the C-O bond in ethers breaks forming alcohol and alkyl iodide. An ether has an oxygen between two carbon groups, C-O-C.

q: Ethoxyethane was used for many years as a surgical _____ agent but has now been replaced by safer nonflammable alternatives.
e: Ethoxyethane was used for many years as a surgical anaesthetic agent but has now been replaced by safer nonflammable alternatives. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Aldehydes and ketones are organic compounds which contain the _____ group.
e: Aldehydes and ketones are organic compounds which contain the carbonyl group. An aldehyde has a carbonyl carbon attached to at least one hydrogen.

q: In aldehydes, a carbonyl group located at the end of a carbon chain is bonded to at least one _____ atom.
e: In aldehydes, a carbonyl group located at the end of a carbon chain is bonded to at least one hydrogen atom. An aldehyde has a carbonyl carbon attached to at least one hydrogen.

q: Aldehydes and ketones have the general formula _____.
e: Aldehydes and ketones have the general formula CnH2nO. An aldehyde has a carbonyl carbon attached to at least one hydrogen.

q: In the IUPAC system for aldehydes, the suffix _____ instead of -e is added to the characteristic stem.
e: In the IUPAC system for aldehydes, the suffix -al instead of -e is added to the characteristic stem. An aldehyde has a carbonyl carbon attached to at least one hydrogen.

q: Primary and secondary alcohols give aldehydes and ketones respectively when gently heated with an oxidising agent such as acidified _____ solution.
e: Primary and secondary alcohols give aldehydes and ketones respectively when gently heated with an oxidising agent such as acidified potassium dichromate solution. In a secondary alcohol the carbon that holds OH is attached to two other carbons.

q: To make the aldehyde, the primary alcohol is heated gently and the product is obtained by _____ to remove it immediately.
e: To make the aldehyde, the primary alcohol is heated gently and the product is obtained by distillation to remove it immediately. In a primary alcohol the carbon that holds OH is attached to only one other carbon, or it is CH3OH.

q: The addition of water to ethyne in the presence of $H_2SO_4$ and _____ produces ethanal.
e: The addition of water to ethyne in the presence of H2SO4 and HgSO4 produces ethanal. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: At room temperature, methanal is a gas and ethanal is a volatile _____.
e: At room temperature, methanal is a gas and ethanal is a volatile liquid. Higher temperature means a larger fraction of particles have energy at least Ea.

q: Aldehydes are easily oxidised to carboxylic acids, but ketones are generally oxidised only under _____ conditions.
e: Aldehydes are easily oxidised to carboxylic acids, but ketones are generally oxidised only under vigorous conditions. Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group and are typically weak acids.

q: Aldehydes and ketones are easily reduced to the corresponding alcohols using the reducing agent _____ in dry ether.
e: Aldehydes and ketones are easily reduced to the corresponding alcohols using the reducing agent LiAlH4 in dry ether. Ethers have an oxygen bridged between two carbon groups and are often used as solvents.

q: Hydrogen cyanide, HCN, adds across the carbon-oxygen double bond in aldehydes and some ketones to produce compounds known as _____.
e: Hydrogen cyanide, HCN, adds across the carbon-oxygen double bond in aldehydes and some ketones to produce compounds known as hydroxynitriles. An aldehyde has a carbonyl carbon attached to at least one hydrogen.

q: Formalin, a 40% aqueous solution of _____, is used as a disinfectant and a preservative for biological specimens.
e: Formalin, a 40% aqueous solution of methanal, is used as a disinfectant and a preservative for biological specimens. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Carboxylic acids are organic compounds with a carboxyl functional group _____.
e: Carboxylic acids are organic compounds with a carboxyl functional group -COOH. A functional group is the reactive atom grouping that sets the chemistry of an organic family.

q: The carboxyl group is made up of a carbonyl group and a _____ group.
e: The carboxyl group is made up of a carbonyl group and a hydroxyl group. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Carboxylic acids form a homologous series with the general formula _____.
e: Carboxylic acids form a homologous series with the general formula CnH2nO2. Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group and are typically weak acids.

q: Many carboxylic acid members get their common names from the _____ names of their natural sources.
e: Many carboxylic acid members get their common names from the Latin names of their natural sources. Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group and are typically weak acids.

q: In the IUPAC system for carboxylic acids, the -e from the name of the parent chain is replaced by _____.
e: In the IUPAC system for carboxylic acids, the -e from the name of the parent chain is replaced by -oic acid. Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group and are typically weak acids.

q: Since a carboxylic acid group must always be found at the end of a carbon chain, it is always given the '_____' location position in numbering.
e: Since a carboxylic acid group must always be found at the end of a carbon chain, it is always given the '1' location position in numbering. Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group and are typically weak acids.

q: Ethanoic acid can be formed by the oxidation of ethanol using atmospheric oxygen in the presence of the bacteria _____.
e: Ethanoic acid can be formed by the oxidation of ethanol using atmospheric oxygen in the presence of the bacteria Acetobacter. Oxidation state tracks how oxidised an atom is; transition metals often show several values.

q: There are intermolecular hydrogen bonds between carboxylic acid molecules, so they have _____ boiling points compared to other compounds of comparable molecular mass.
e: There are intermolecular hydrogen bonds between carboxylic acid molecules, so they have high boiling points compared to other compounds of comparable molecular mass. Intermolecular forces tug neighbouring molecules or ions together; they are not the bonds inside a molecule.

q: Carboxylic acids are weak acids, and they can react with reactive metals to give salt and _____.
e: Carboxylic acids are weak acids, and they can react with reactive metals to give salt and hydrogen. Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group and are typically weak acids.

q: Carboxylic acids react with carbonates to give salt, water and _____.
e: Carboxylic acids react with carbonates to give salt, water and carbon dioxide. Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group and are typically weak acids.

q: Carboxylic acids are reduced to their corresponding primary alcohols using $LiAlH_4$ in _____ ether at room temperature.
e: Carboxylic acids are reduced to their corresponding primary alcohols using LiAlH4 in dry ether at room temperature. In a primary alcohol the carbon that holds OH is attached to only one other carbon, or it is CH3OH.

q: The popular painkiller, aspirin, is the acetyl derivative of _____ acid.
e: The popular painkiller, aspirin, is the acetyl derivative of salicylic acid. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Esters are carboxylic acid derivatives in which the hydroxyl group has been replaced by an _____ group.
e: Esters are carboxylic acid derivatives in which the hydroxyl group has been replaced by an alkoxy group. Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group and are typically weak acids.

q: The name of an ester is formed by writing the name of the alkyl group followed by the name of the acid with the -ic acid ending replaced by _____.
e: The name of an ester is formed by writing the name of the alkyl group followed by the name of the acid with the -ic acid ending replaced by -ate. An ester has the -COO- link and is often made from an acid plus an alcohol.

q: Generally, carboxylic acid can react with alcohol to form ester in a process which is known as _____.
e: Generally, carboxylic acid can react with alcohol to form ester in a process which is known as esterification. Saponification: cations form when atoms lose electrons.

q: Carboxylic acid esters of low molecular mass are colourless, volatile liquids with pleasant _____.
e: Carboxylic acid esters of low molecular mass are colourless, volatile liquids with pleasant odours. Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group and are typically weak acids.

q: Acidic hydrolysis of an ester is simply the _____ of esterification.
e: Acidic hydrolysis of an ester is simply the reverse of esterification. Esterification is the reaction of an alcohol with an acid to make an ester and water.

q: When an ester is refluxed with an alkali, it is fully hydrolysed to form an alcohol and the _____ salt of the carboxylic acid.
e: When an ester is refluxed with an alkali, it is fully hydrolysed to form an alcohol and the sodium salt of the carboxylic acid. Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group and are typically weak acids.

q: The most common method of transesterification is the reaction of the ester with an alcohol in the presence of an _____ catalyst.
e: The most common method of transesterification is the reaction of the ester with an alcohol in the presence of an acid catalyst. Transesterification swaps the alkoxy group of an ester with an alcohol to make a different ester.

q: Naturally-occurring esters mixed with NaOH produce _____ that is used for washing dishes and clothes.
e: Naturally-occurring esters mixed with NaOH produce soap that is used for washing dishes and clothes. An ester has the -COO- link and is often made from an acid plus an alcohol.

q: An amine is a compound in which one or more hydrogen atoms of _____ have been replaced by alkyl groups.
e: An amine is a compound in which one or more hydrogen atoms of ammonia have been replaced by alkyl groups. Ammonia: amines are organic bases with a nitrogen that can accept a proton.

q: Amines are classified as primary, secondary, and tertiary depending on how many _____ groups are attached to the nitrogen.
e: Amines are classified as primary, secondary, and tertiary depending on how many alkyl groups are attached to the nitrogen. An amine is an organic base with nitrogen that can accept a proton.

q: In the IUPAC system for amines, the -e from the name of the parent chain is replaced by _____.
e: In the IUPAC system for amines, the -e from the name of the parent chain is replaced by -amine. Amines are organic bases with a nitrogen that can accept a proton.

q: Ethanamine is prepared by heating bromoethane with an excess of ammonia dissolved in _____.
e: Ethanamine is prepared by heating bromoethane with an excess of ammonia dissolved in ethanol. An amine is an organic base with nitrogen that can accept a proton.

q: Excess hot ethanolic ammonia is used in amine preparation to avoid the formation of secondary and tertiary amines and _____ salts.
e: Excess hot ethanolic ammonia is used in amine preparation to avoid the formation of secondary and tertiary amines and ammonium salts. Amines are organic bases with a nitrogen that can accept a proton.

q: Liquid amines possess a _____ smell.
e: Liquid amines possess a fishy smell. An amine is an organic base with nitrogen that can accept a proton.

q: Primary and secondary amines have higher boiling points than alkanes because they can form an intermolecular _____ bonding.
e: Primary and secondary amines have higher boiling points than alkanes because they can form an intermolecular hydrogen bonding. Intermolecular forces tug neighbouring molecules or ions together; they are not the bonds inside a molecule.

q: Ethanamine reacts with chloroform in the presence of an alkali to form ethyl isocyanide with an unpleasant smell, known as the _____ reaction.
e: Ethanamine reacts with chloroform in the presence of an alkali to form ethyl isocyanide with an unpleasant smell, known as the carbylamine reaction. An amine is an organic base with nitrogen that can accept a proton.

q: Amides are carboxylic acid derivatives in which the -OH of the carboxylic acid has been replaced by an _____ group.
e: Amides are carboxylic acid derivatives in which the -OH of the carboxylic acid has been replaced by an amine group. Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group and are typically weak acids.

q: Amides are named as derivatives of the corresponding carboxylic acids, the suffix -amide being substituted for _____ in the name of the parent acid.
e: Amides are named as derivatives of the corresponding carboxylic acids, the suffix -amide being substituted for -oic acid in the name of the parent acid. Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group and are typically weak acids.

q: The addition of ammonia to a carboxylic acid forms an amide via a _____ reaction, as water is eliminated.
e: The addition of ammonia to a carboxylic acid forms an amide via a condensation reaction, as water is eliminated. Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group and are typically weak acids.

q: Like esters, aqueous solutions of amides are usually _____.
e: Like esters, aqueous solutions of amides are usually neutral. An ester has the -COO- link and is often made from an acid plus an alcohol.

q: If an amide is refluxed with hydrochloric acid, the products are the corresponding carboxylic acid and a primary _____.
e: If an amide is refluxed with hydrochloric acid, the products are the corresponding carboxylic acid and a primary amine. Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group and are typically weak acids.

q: Amides such as nylon are used in textiles, to produce ropes, bulletproof vests and _____ cords.
e: Amides such as nylon are used in textiles, to produce ropes, bulletproof vests and tyre cords. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The groups of atoms that are attached to the carbon backbone of organic compounds are known as _____ groups.
e: The groups of atoms that are attached to the carbon backbone of organic compounds are known as functional groups. Kb is the base dissociation constant; larger Kb means a stronger weak base.

q: The most common functional groups in organic compounds other than hydrocarbons include carbonyl, hydroxyl, carboxyl, carboalkoxy, amine and _____.
e: The most common functional groups in organic compounds other than hydrocarbons include carbonyl, hydroxyl, carboxyl, carboalkoxy, amine and carboxamide. A functional group is the reactive atom grouping that sets the chemistry of an organic family.

q: A chemical test is typically a fast reaction performed in a test tube that gives a visual clue such as a colour change, precipitate, or _____ formation.
e: A chemical test is typically a fast reaction performed in a test tube that gives a visual clue such as a colour change, precipitate, or gas formation. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Alkenes mixed with 1% $KMnO_4$ solution will result in _____.
e: Alkenes mixed with 1% KMnO4 solution will result in decolourisation. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Alkynes passed through ammoniacal $Cu_2Cl_2$ solution will form a _____ coloured precipitate.
e: Alkynes passed through ammoniacal Cu2Cl2 solution will form a red coloured precipitate. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Alcohols warmed with acidified $K_2Cr_2O_7$ solution will change from orange colour to _____ colour.
e: Alcohols warmed with acidified K2Cr2O7 solution will change from orange colour to green colour. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Ethers boiled with HI and then reacted with $AgNO_3$ will form a _____ coloured precipitate.
e: Ethers boiled with HI and then reacted with AgNO3 will form a yellow coloured precipitate. An ether has an oxygen between two carbon groups, C-O-C.

q: Aldehydes heated gently with Fehling's solution will form a _____ coloured precipitate.
e: Aldehydes heated gently with Fehling's solution will form a reddish-brown coloured precipitate. An aldehyde has a carbonyl carbon attached to at least one hydrogen.

q: Ketones mixed with 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine (2,4-DNP) solution will form a _____ coloured precipitate.
e: Ketones mixed with 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine (2,4-DNP) solution will form a deep-orange coloured precipitate. A ketone has a carbonyl carbon attached to two carbon groups.

q: Carboxylic acids mixed with saturated $NaHCO_3$ solution will result in the evolution of _____.
e: Carboxylic acids mixed with saturated NaHCO3 solution will result in the evolution of CO2. Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group and are typically weak acids.

q: Esters heated gently with EtOH, phenolphthalein and dilute NaOH will result in _____.
e: Esters heated gently with EtOH, phenolphthalein and dilute NaOH will result in decolourisation. An ester has the -COO- link and is often made from an acid plus an alcohol.

q: Primary amines reacted with $CHCl_3$ in the presence of alkali will produce an _____.
e: Primary amines reacted with CHCl3 in the presence of alkali will produce an unpleasant smell. An amine is an organic base with nitrogen that can accept a proton.

q: Primary amides boiled with 20% NaOH solution will result in the evolution of _____.
e: Primary amides boiled with 20% NaOH solution will result in the evolution of NH3. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The presence of a carbonyl group such as aldehyde or ketone can be easily tested by using a solution of _____.
e: The presence of a carbonyl group such as aldehyde or ketone can be easily tested by using a solution of 2,4-DNP. Aldehydes have a carbonyl carbon attached to at least one hydrogen.

q: Fehling's solution is an alkaline solution containing copper(_____) ions.
e: Fehling's solution is an alkaline solution containing copper(II) ions. Ka is the acid dissociation constant; larger Ka means a stronger weak acid.

q: Fehling's solution can be used to distinguish aldehyde and ketone functional groups because aldehydes can be further oxidised to form _____ acids.
e: Fehling's solution can be used to distinguish aldehyde and ketone functional groups because aldehydes can be further oxidised to form carboxylic acids. A functional group is the reactive atom grouping that sets the chemistry of an organic family.

q: Infrared (IR) spectroscopy is the study of the absorption of light by a compound, in the _____ region of the electromagnetic spectrum.
e: Infrared (IR) spectroscopy is the study of the absorption of light by a compound, in the infrared region of the electromagnetic spectrum. Infrared spectroscopy identifies groups by the frequencies of light they absorb as bonds vibrate.

q: The relationship between the energy (E) and the frequency of electromagnetic radiation is described by _____ equation.
e: The relationship between the energy (E) and the frequency of electromagnetic radiation is described by Planck's equation. Frequency is how many wave crests pass a point each second.

q: Wavenumber, which is the reciprocal of the wavelength, is measured in _____.
e: Wavenumber, which is the reciprocal of the wavelength, is measured in cm-1. Wavenumber counts how many waves fit into one centimetre.

q: High frequencies, large wavenumbers, and short wavelengths are associated with _____ energies.
e: High frequencies, large wavenumbers, and short wavelengths are associated with high energies. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Photons in the infrared radiation region can cause bond _____ in molecules.
e: Photons in the infrared radiation region can cause bond vibrations in molecules. Infrared spectroscopy identifies groups by the frequencies of light they absorb as bonds vibrate.

q: Stretching is a vibration that occurs along the bond line and changes the bond _____.
e: Stretching is a vibration that occurs along the bond line and changes the bond length. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Only those stretching and bending motions that change the _____ moment of a molecule give rise to the absorption of infrared radiation.
e: Only those stretching and bending motions that change the dipole moment of a molecule give rise to the absorption of infrared radiation. Infrared spectroscopy identifies groups by the frequencies of light they absorb as bonds vibrate.

q: Homonuclear diatomic molecules such as $N_2$ which have no dipole moments are IR _____.
e: Homonuclear diatomic molecules such as N2 which have no dipole moments are IR inactive. Dipole moment measures how polar a bond or molecule is.

q: Light atoms vibrate at _____ frequencies than heavier atoms.
e: Light atoms vibrate at higher frequencies than heavier atoms. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: It takes more energy to _____ a bond than to bend it.
e: It takes more energy to stretch a bond than to bend it. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The instrument used to obtain an infrared spectrum is called an IR _____.
e: The instrument used to obtain an infrared spectrum is called an IR spectrometer. Infrared spectroscopy identifies groups by the frequencies of light they absorb as bonds vibrate.

q: An IR spectrum is a plot of the percent transmittance or absorbance of radiation versus the _____ of the radiation transmitted.
e: An IR spectrum is a plot of the percent transmittance or absorbance of radiation versus the wavenumber of the radiation transmitted. Wavenumber counts how many waves fit into one centimetre.

q: The O-H bond of alcohols usually has an absorption in the range of _____ $cm^{-1}$.
e: The O-H bond of alcohols usually has an absorption in the range of 3200-3600 cm-1. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The O-H bond of carboxylic acids occurs in the range of _____ $cm^{-1}$.
e: The O-H bond of carboxylic acids occurs in the range of 2500-3300 cm-1. Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group and are typically weak acids.

q: The broad shape of the O-H absorption band results from the _____ bonding of the OH groups between molecules.
e: The broad shape of the O-H absorption band results from the hydrogen bonding of the OH groups between molecules. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: N-H stretches in amine and amide are of medium intensity and width, and appear in the range of _____ $cm^{-1}$.
e: N-H stretches in amine and amide are of medium intensity and width, and appear in the range of 3300-3500 cm-1. Amines are organic bases with a nitrogen that can accept a proton.

q: A macromolecule is a very large molecule that contains thousands of atoms or more, because 'macro' means _____.
e: A macromolecule is a very large molecule that contains thousands of atoms or more, because 'macro' means large. The because-clause is the chemical reason that makes the statement hold.

q: A polymer is a type of long-chain macromolecule that is linked together by many small repeat units known as _____.
e: A polymer is a type of long-chain macromolecule that is linked together by many small repeat units known as monomers. A polymer is a giant molecule made by linking many small monomer units.

q: If a polymer consists of only one kind of monomers then it is called a _____.
e: If a polymer consists of only one kind of monomers then it is called a homopolymer. A copolymer uses two or more monomers.

q: A polymer which consists of more than one kind of monomers is called a _____.
e: A polymer which consists of more than one kind of monomers is called a copolymer. A homopolymer uses only one monomer.

q: The process of joining together a large number of monomers to form a polymer is called _____.
e: The process of joining together a large number of monomers to form a polymer is called polymerisation. A polymer is a giant molecule made by linking many small monomer units.

q: Addition polymerisation occurs when unsaturated monomers join together without losing any molecules or _____.
e: Addition polymerisation occurs when unsaturated monomers join together without losing any molecules or atoms. Addition polymerisation joins monomers that have C=C double bonds without losing a small molecule.

q: Condensation polymerisation occurs when the monomers combine to form a polymer, with the removal of a small molecule such as _____.
e: Condensation polymerisation occurs when the monomers combine to form a polymer, with the removal of a small molecule such as water. Condensation polymerisation joins monomers and knocks out a small molecule such as water.

q: The simplest addition polymer is polyethene, which is produced by the addition polymerisation of _____ monomers.
e: The simplest addition polymer is polyethene, which is produced by the addition polymerisation of ethene monomers. Addition polymerisation joins monomers that have C=C double bonds without losing a small molecule.

q: In polyalkenes made of one type of monomer, the repeat unit is the same as the monomer except that the carbon-carbon double bond is changed to a carbon-carbon _____ bond.
e: In polyalkenes made of one type of monomer, the repeat unit is the same as the monomer except that the carbon-carbon double bond is changed to a carbon-carbon single bond. A monomer is a small reactive molecule that joins again and again to build a polymer.

q: Polychloroethene is also commonly known as polyvinyl chloride or _____.
e: Polychloroethene is also commonly known as polyvinyl chloride or PVC. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: At low temperatures, addition polymers lose plasticity and elasticity and become _____.
e: At low temperatures, addition polymers lose plasticity and elasticity and become brittle. Higher temperature means a larger fraction of particles have energy at least Ea.

q: Many frying pans are coated with a layer of _____, which is heat-resistant and has non-stick properties.
e: Many frying pans are coated with a layer of nylon, which is heat-resistant and has non-stick properties. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Polystyrene is hard, light and brittle, and is also known as _____.
e: Polystyrene is hard, light and brittle, and is also known as styrofoam. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Condensation polymerisation is characterised by monomers that contain two different _____ groups.
e: Condensation polymerisation is characterised by monomers that contain two different functional groups. Condensation polymerisation joins monomers and knocks out a small molecule such as water.

q: Terylene or polyethylene terephthalate (PET) is formed from the reaction of terephthalic acid and _____.
e: Terylene or polyethylene terephthalate (PET) is formed from the reaction of terephthalic acid and propane-1,2-diol. pH is the negative log of [H+], so a smaller pH means a more acidic solution.

q: In the condensation polymerisation of polyesters, a hydrogen atom is lost from the alcohol, and a _____ group is lost from the carboxylic acid.
e: In the condensation polymerisation of polyesters, a hydrogen atom is lost from the alcohol, and a hydroxyl group is lost from the carboxylic acid. Condensation polymerisation joins monomers and knocks out a small molecule such as water.

q: Terylene is a polyester as it contains many _____ linkages.
e: Terylene is a polyester as it contains many ester linkages. An ester has the -COO- link and is often made from an acid plus an alcohol.

q: Nylon 6,6 is formed from the reaction of adipic acid and _____.
e: Nylon 6,6 is formed from the reaction of adipic acid and 1,6-diaminohexane. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: In the formation of polyamides, a new bond is formed between nitrogen and carbon atoms to form an _____ linkage.
e: In the formation of polyamides, a new bond is formed between nitrogen and carbon atoms to form an amide linkage. Ka is the acid dissociation constant; larger Ka means a stronger weak acid.

q: A large protein molecule is one of the types of _____.
e: A large protein molecule is one of the types of polyamides. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The general formula of amino acid is _____.
e: The general formula of amino acid is H2NCHRCOOH. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The covalent bond formed between two amino acids is called a _____ bond.
e: The covalent bond formed between two amino acids is called a peptide bond. A covalent bond is a shared pair of electrons between atoms.

q: An amino acid unit within a polypeptide chain is called an amino acid _____.
e: An amino acid unit within a polypeptide chain is called an amino acid residue. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Condensation polymers often have _____ molecular masses than addition polymers.
e: Condensation polymers often have lower molecular masses than addition polymers. A polymer is a long chain made by linking many small monomers.

q: The presence of polar functional groups on polymer chains often enhances chain-chain attractions, and thus, crystallinity and _____ strength increase.
e: The presence of polar functional groups on polymer chains often enhances chain-chain attractions, and thus, crystallinity and tensile strength increase. A functional group is the reactive atom grouping that sets the chemistry of an organic family.

q: Terylene is resistant to stretching and shrinking, and is used more and more in _____.
e: Terylene is resistant to stretching and shrinking, and is used more and more in textiles. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Since plastics are non-biodegradable, they cannot be broken down by _____ in the soil.
e: Since plastics are non-biodegradable, they cannot be broken down by bacteria in the soil. Biodegradable plastics can be broken down by microorganisms.

q: Upon incineration, PVC produces corrosive _____ gas.
e: Upon incineration, PVC produces corrosive hydrogen chloride gas. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Plastics that are thrown into the sea endanger marine animals, and may clog up rivers and drains, increasing _____.
e: Plastics that are thrown into the sea endanger marine animals, and may clog up rivers and drains, increasing flooding. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: To aid in the separation of plastics for recycling, manufacturers require to place a recycling _____ on their products.
e: To aid in the separation of plastics for recycling, manufacturers require to place a recycling symbol on their products. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The lower the number in the middle of the recycling symbol, the _____ is the ease with which the material can be recycled.
e: The lower the number in the middle of the recycling symbol, the greater is the ease with which the material can be recycled. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The recycling symbol (1) PETE/PET stands for polyethylene _____.
e: The recycling symbol (1) PETE/PET stands for polyethylene terephthalate. pH is the negative log of [H+], so a smaller pH means a more acidic solution.

q: Biodegradable plastics should contain small amounts of _____ granules to degrade naturally by microorganisms.
e: Biodegradable plastics should contain small amounts of starch granules to degrade naturally by microorganisms. Biodegradable plastics can be broken down by microorganisms.

q: Polylactic acid (PLA) is made from fermented plant starch, usually _____.
e: Polylactic acid (PLA) is made from fermented plant starch, usually corn. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Photodegradable plastics incorporate _____ groups at intervals down their length to absorb energy from ultraviolet rays.
e: Photodegradable plastics incorporate carbonyl groups at intervals down their length to absorb energy from ultraviolet rays. Photodegradable plastics slowly break down in light.
